statement: You are given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order.
Rearrange nums in place so that each distinct value appears exactly once, in the original order, at the front of the array. What remains after those positions does not matter.
Return k, the number of distinct values; after the call, nums[0..k − 1] must hold them.

examples.explanation: The distinct values are 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4, so k = 5 and they occupy nums[0..4].
No value repeats, so every element stays where it is and k = 5.

constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
